concept: Big total, no win. The hero sets the paradox in two tones: India's 720 in muted grey, the twist in white ('New Zealand still saved the Test'), with the final 239/5 and the three day-5 wickets underneath. Slide 2 turns the rearguard into a bar chart of balls faced, not runs: Mitchell's glowing 186-ball bar leads three grey bars for Conway, Ravindra and Phillips, because on a final day time matters more than runs. Slide 3 is one giant number (120 runs in a whole day) that shows how little NZ needed to score. Slide 4 is the 'so close' timeline (Blundell's DRS wicket, Akash Deep's missed run-out) and the last slide points to Christchurch and hands fans the declaration debate. Cricket blue, pitch lines and type only: no player photos, no logos.
caption:
India made 720. New Zealand still walked away with a draw.

The Wellington Test ended on Monday with New Zealand on 239 for 5 in 120 overs. They began the final day on 119 for 2 and needed to survive, not score.

Why it worked: Daryl Mitchell faced 186 balls for 49 not out. Glenn Phillips faced 126 balls for 26 not out. India took three wickets on the day (Conway, Ravindra and Blundell) but none after Blundell fell in the 77th over. Akash Deep also missed a run-out chance on Mitchell.

The two-Test series stays level. The second Test starts in Christchurch on Friday.
